subject: Spanska
title: Family and numbers
sourceSummary: Family words, possession with possessive pronouns, and the numbers 0–100.

questions.opener: Compare it with "hermano", which you may already know.
questions.explanation: "Hermana" means sister. "Hermano" (with -o) means brother — Spanish often changes the ending -o/-a to show gender.

questions.opener: The plural word covers both sides of the family.
questions.explanation: "Abuelo" is grandfather and "abuela" is grandmother. "Abuelos" in the plural means grandparents together.

questions.prompt: Choose the right word: "___ madre se llama Rosa." (My mom is named Rosa.)
questions.opener: Possessive pronouns in Spanish also follow gender and number.
questions.explanation: "Mi" means "my" in the singular and fits with "madre" (mom). "Mis" is plural ("my", for several things), "tu" is "your", and "su" is "his/her".

questions.prompt: How do you write the number 15 in letters?
questions.opener: 15 is one of the irregular numbers between 11 and 15.
Numbers from 30 up are built as "tens + y + ones".
questions.explanation: "Treinta" is 30 and "siete" is 7, joined with "y" (and): "treinta y siete" = 37.

questions.opener: It's the round number after noventa y nueve (99).

questions.prompt: Correct the error: "Mi hermano se llama Sofía y tiene catorce años." (The name refers to a girl.)
questions.opener: The word for brother versus sister changes with gender.
questions.answer: Mi hermana se llama Sofía y tiene catorce años.
steps: Sofía is a girl's name, so it should be "hermana" (sister), not "hermano" (brother).
The rest of the sentence is correct: "se llama Sofía" (is named Sofía) and "tiene catorce años" (is fourteen years old) are conjugated correctly.
Remember: Spanish nouns for family members almost always follow the person's gender through the ending -o/-a.

questions.prompt: Which family words, possessive pronouns, and numbers should you know at the grade 7 level in Spanish?
questions.opener: The family, who it belongs to, and counting to a hundred.
questions.answer: Family: madre/padre = mom/dad · hermano/hermana = brother/sister · abuelo/abuela = grandfather/grandmother · hijo/hija = son/daughter · primo/prima = cousin. Possessives: mi/mis = my (sg/pl) · tu/tus = your (sg/pl) · su/sus = his/her/their. Numbers: 0 cero, 1 uno, 5 cinco, 10 diez, 11 once, 15 quince, 20 veinte, 21 veintiuno, 30 treinta, 37 treinta y siete, 50 cincuenta, 100 cien.
